Team — looked at Nimbus's redline. My proposed positions below (keeping business close to their ask while limiting risk):

1) Backup/DR exception (proposed language):
"Notwithstanding any deletion/retention obligations in this Agreement, Redwood may retain copies of Customer Data in encrypted backups strictly for the purposes of disaster recovery, incident investigation, or lawful retention obligations for a period not to exceed 90 days. Extension beyond 90 days up to a maximum of 180 days may be permitted only upon written agreement between the parties documenting the necessity and scope of extended retention; in all cases, retained backups will remain subject to the security obligations of this DPA."

Rationale: 90 days default minimizes exposure; the 180-day extension is allowed but requires written justification. This addresses Nimbus's ask for 180 days while preserving control.

2) Subprocessors & transfers: provide current subprocessor list (public link) and commit to 30-days notice before onboarding major subprocessors handling Customer Data. Include SCCs for EU transfers and a data transfer addendum reference. Dev — can you publish the snapshot link to the subprocessor list and confirm the process for notifications?

If we agree, I can run a final DPA with these edits and send to Nimbus for signature via DocuSign.

-Rishi
General Counsel | Redwood Inference

Hi Lara / Soojin — thanks. Following up with operational details to include in the DPA: 

- Backups are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and access-controlled; only a small ops on-call group can trigger restores.
- Forensic copies: we will log and document all access to retained backup copies, and we will provide an audit summary to Nimbus on request.
- Deletion/long-term retention: we will implement an automated job to purge backup snapshots older than the agreed retention window unless a hold is placed via formal request (we'll capture the hold request process in the DPA).

Suggested clause addendum: "Redwood will maintain documented procedures for backup encryption, access controls, and retention schedules. Upon Customer request, Redwood will provide a summary of backup access and any holds placed for recovery or investigation purposes."

I can fold this into the final redline.

-Neha
